A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSC and contrastive fine-tuning study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations and transfer results on Bongard OpenWorld, Bongard-HOI and Winoground.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds VQA evaluations, representation visualizations and a loss-scheduling sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The nearest-centroid LSC probe, PEFT interventions and combined contrastive/next-token objective remain unchanged. The dual cosine schedule foregrounded in v3 already appears, with the same equations and stated use, in v2 Appendix F, now Appendix I.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix A adds POPE, A-OKVQA and ScienceQA evaluations, plus a single-image multiple-choice adaptation of Bongard-HOI. This substantially extends task coverage beyond the retained Bongard rule-induction and Winoground retrieval evaluations.

E2.justification: The new VQA comparison introduces a simulated random-answer baseline alongside CLIP probing and untuned, next-token-trained and combined-loss Phi models. Comparator membership in the matched Bongard, PEFT, probing and Winoground experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify four-option construction for HOI/POPE, zero-shot VQA prompting without CoT, and a constant-versus-dual-cosine loss-weight sweep evaluated on ID/OOD prompts and Winoground. The existing Bongard splits, checkpoint selection and core fine-tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds PCA and Isomap analyses of representation geometry and a quantitative Phi-HOI loss-scheduling sensitivity study. Conversely, v2 Appendix K's per-class imbalance investigation is removed. Existing vision-encoder ablations, prompt-format robustness, HOI novelty splits and attention analyses remain after relocation.

E5.justification: V3 newly identifies the sensitivity sweep as using a fixed seed and adds an unspecified cross-seed consistency assertion. It clarifies that the chi-squared analysis concerns paired trial-level correctness. Margins of error disappear from two main tables but remain in matching appendix tables; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: V3 adds VQA, sensitivity and geometric findings. For example, new Table A.1 reports 78.89%, 67.57% and 54.53% for baseline, next-token-trained and combined-loss Phi on converted multiple-choice HOI. Retained Bongard and Winoground scores are unchanged. V2's strategy-count table and per-class result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The centroid construction, contrastive-loss definition and cosine scheduling equations are retained. The new injectivity and manifold discussion provides conceptual motivation and interpretation, without introducing a formal theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: V3 recasts the abstract's dormant-reasoning activation claim as one-dimensional visual-manifold restructuring for image comparison on abstract binary classification tasks. Its conclusion foregrounds the existing dual cosine schedule and a new geometry-to-transfer claim, replacing v2's broader emphasis on resolving the alignment gap through robust, transferable reasoning.

C2.justification: V3 interprets accuracy convergence as redirecting nonlinear computation toward representation refinement, replacing v2's contrastive-ceiling interpretation. It adds semantic-ray and information-accessibility explanations, and interprets VQA and prompt-format failures as renewed image-to-text misalignment. V2 primarily emphasized catastrophic forgetting and syntactic overfitting.

D1.justification: V3 documents the new VQA question conversion and sensitivity-grid settings, but removes v2's explicit balanced-test-set disclosure. Existing LoRA and prompt hyperparameters, embedding extraction procedures and scheduling formulas remain available, often relocated. The new extraction flowchart mainly illustrates previously documented steps.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for POPE, A-OKVQA, ScienceQA and Nikolaou et al.'s transformer-injectivity work. The latter supplies new positioning around preserved information versus accessible representations. The existing related-work discussion and image-to-image alignment positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The main argument is extensively reorganized around diagnosing the gap, enhancing generation and connecting the two reasoning pathways. V3 rewrites the abstract and conclusion, creates a dedicated discussion section, moves the LLM-usage disclosure to the end and reorders the appendices.

P2.justification: V3 adds diagnostic and extraction schematics, PCA/Isomap displays, and VQA and sensitivity tables; it removes the strategy-count and per-class tables. Main tables are reformatted and scatter-plot labels and legends revised. Existing attention-map images are retained, with expanded captions and redistributed placement.

improvement.justification: The new VQA failures provide stronger evidence for applicability limits and support v3's more specific visual-alignment claims. Geometry and sensitivity analyses also improve explanation. These gains are tempered by removal of the per-class diagnostic and weaknesses in the fixed-seed sensitivity analysis: Appendix N calls the probe trend monotonic despite the reversal between weights 0.4 and 0.8 in Table A.9. The net quality gain is modest.
